{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement changes within the existing Spring XD architecture and conventions represented by the referenced branch, rather than introducing a new platform or major framework migration.",
    "For reliable HDFS writes, expose acknowledgement only after the configured HDFS commit operation succeeds, while preserving an opt-in mode so existing stream behavior remains backward compatible.",
    "Implement source and processor partition overrides through a configurable partitioning strategy or function, with the existing default partition behavior retained when no override is supplied.",
    "Model multiple topic-partitions as a collection of consumer endpoints behind one logical input/queue, with explicit configuration and validation for assigned topic-partitions.",
    "Implement the new DSL parser as a context-aware parse/validation component that can resolve stream references across separately parsed DSL fragments.",
    "Treat single-container stream deployment as an architectural design and documentation deliverable, not a full production implementation, unless existing components can support a small demonstrator without significant redesign.",
    "Preserve non-default ConfigurableConversionService instances as part of tuple serialization/deserialization context rather than replacing them with the framework default.",
    "Use repeatable benchmark scenarios with identical workload, data volume, JVM settings, and stream topology for JMX-enabled and JMX-disabled comparisons.",
    "Add automated unit and integration tests for each behavior, while retaining compatibility tests for existing default behavior."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The referenced source repository and branch are available, buildable, and use an established test framework and continuous integration setup.",
    "The increment is implemented by one experienced Java/Spring developer; estimates represent hands-on work-hours and exclude elapsed calendar time.",
    "Requirements do not include production rollout, operational support, migration of existing deployments, or extensive UI development.",
    "Existing HDFS, messaging, module, parser, tuple serialization, and deployment abstractions can be extended without replacing their underlying technologies.",
    "Reliable HDFS acknowledgement is required for stream pipelines but may be implemented as a configurable delivery or sink mode to avoid breaking existing users.",
    "The partition override API may be configuration-based or module-code-based, provided source and processor modules can supply a deterministic partition function.",
    "Multiple topic-partition consumption is limited to the existing supported messaging technology and does not require cross-broker transactional guarantees.",
    "The DSL parser must validate module and option references and stream names, but does not need to provide a complete new Flo UI implementation.",
    "The single-container deployment work produces an agreed design, deployment model, and documentation with a limited proof of feasibility; it does not deliver a fully hardened container orchestrator.",
    "Benchmarking uses a representative existing stream and synthetic or controlled input data; performance results are documented but no target percentage improvement is prescribed.",
    "Code review, local build troubleshooting, and ordinary regression testing are included in the estimates; major unrelated defects discovered in the baseline are excluded."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Repository analysis and implementation planning",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the referenced branch, identify affected modules and extension points, understand existing tests and build conventions, refine the implementation approach for U1-U8, and establish a test and integration plan.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "BaseDefinition module-list removal and reparsing",
      "activity_description": "Experiment with removing the stored module list from BaseDefinition, implement reparsing or lazy reconstruction where required, update dependent code, and add tests covering deployment and parsing behavior.",
      "most_likely_effort": 28
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Reliable HDFS write acknowledgements",
      "activity_description": "Trace the stream write and message-bus acknowledgement paths, implement an opt-in acknowledgement mode tied to successful HDFS commit completion, handle failures and retries consistently, and add unit and integration coverage.",
      "most_likely_effort": 56
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Source and processor partition-function overrides",
      "activity_description": "Define the override configuration or API, integrate it into source and processor partition routing, preserve default partitioning, validate invalid configurations, and test deterministic routing to selected partitions.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Multiple topic-partition consumption",
      "activity_description": "Extend consumer configuration and runtime management to consume multiple topic-partitions through one logical queue, handle lifecycle and offset behavior, validate configuration, and add integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Context-aware DSL parser",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement parsing that retains stream and module context across separately supplied DSL fragments, resolve references such as taps to previously declared streams, produce useful validation errors, and add parser and endpoint tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Single-container stream deployment design",
      "activity_description": "Analyze module colocation requirements, define the proposed container and lifecycle model, identify configuration, networking, resource, and failure-handling implications, create a feasibility prototype or deployment sketch where practical, and document the approach.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Uniform handling of non-default conversion services",
      "activity_description": "Trace tuple serialization and deserialization, preserve non-default ConfigurableConversionService instances or their equivalent configuration, update affected transport paths, and add regression tests proving the service is not reset.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "JMX performance benchmark and documentation",
      "activity_description": "Prepare repeatable streams and workload generation, execute controlled JMX-enabled and JMX-disabled runs, collect and analyze throughput, latency, and resource measurements, and document methodology and results.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature integration and regression testing",
      "activity_description": "Run the full build and test suite, add cross-feature integration scenarios, investigate and fix regressions, verify backward compatibility of default modes, and validate behavior in representative deployment configurations.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Code review preparation and delivery documentation",
      "activity_description": "Refactor for maintainability, update configuration and API documentation, prepare release notes or migration notes, perform final review cleanup, and package the completed increment for handoff.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 364
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement changes within the existing Spring XD architecture and conventions represented by the referenced branch, rather than introducing a new platform or major framework migration.
For reliable HDFS writes, expose acknowledgement only after the configured HDFS commit operation succeeds, while preserving an opt-in mode so existing stream behavior remains backward compatible.
Implement source and processor partition overrides through a configurable partitioning strategy or function, with the existing default partition behavior retained when no override is supplied.
Model multiple topic-partitions as a collection of consumer endpoints behind one logical input/queue, with explicit configuration and validation for assigned topic-partitions.
Implement the new DSL parser as a context-aware parse/validation component that can resolve stream references across separately parsed DSL fragments.

Treat single-container stream deployment as an architectural design and documentation deliverable, not a full production implementation, unless existing components can support a small demonstrator without significant redesign.
Preserve non-default ConfigurableConversionService instances as part of tuple serialization/deserialization context rather than replacing them with the framework default.
Use repeatable benchmark scenarios with identical workload, data volume, JVM settings, and stream topology for JMX-enabled and JMX-disabled comparisons.
Add automated unit and integration tests for each behavior, while retaining compatibility tests for existing default behavior.
assumptions: The referenced source repository and branch are available, buildable, and use an established test framework and continuous integration setup.
The increment is implemented by one experienced Java/Spring developer; estimates represent hands-on work-hours and exclude elapsed calendar time.
Requirements do not include production rollout, operational support, migration of existing deployments, or extensive UI development.
Existing HDFS, messaging, module, parser, tuple serialization, and deployment abstractions can be extended without replacing their underlying technologies.
Reliable HDFS acknowledgement is required for stream pipelines but may be implemented as a configurable delivery or sink mode to avoid breaking existing users.
The partition override API may be configuration-based or module-code-based, provided source and processor modules can supply a deterministic partition function.
Multiple topic-partition consumption is limited to the existing supported messaging technology and does not require cross-broker transactional guarantees.
The DSL parser must validate module and option references and stream names, but does not need to provide a complete new Flo UI implementation.
The single-container deployment work produces an agreed design, deployment model, and documentation with a limited proof of feasibility; it does not deliver a fully hardened container orchestrator.
Benchmarking uses a representative existing stream and synthetic or controlled input data; performance results are documented but no target percentage improvement is prescribed.
Code review, local build troubleshooting, and ordinary regression testing are included in the estimates; major unrelated defects discovered in the baseline are excluded.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the referenced branch, identify affected modules and extension points, understand existing tests and build conventions, refine the implementation approach for U1-U8, and establish a test and integration plan.

Experiment with removing the stored module list from BaseDefinition, implement reparsing or lazy reconstruction where required, update dependent code, and add tests covering deployment and parsing behavior.

Trace the stream write and message-bus acknowledgement paths, implement an opt-in acknowledgement mode tied to successful HDFS commit completion, handle failures and retries consistently, and add unit and integration coverage.

Define the override configuration or API, integrate it into source and processor partition routing, preserve default partitioning, validate invalid configurations, and test deterministic routing to selected partitions.

Extend consumer configuration and runtime management to consume multiple topic-partitions through one logical queue, handle lifecycle and offset behavior, validate configuration, and add integration tests.

Design and implement parsing that retains stream and module context across separately supplied DSL fragments, resolve references such as taps to previously declared streams, produce useful validation errors, and add parser and endpoint tests.

Analyze module colocation requirements, define the proposed container and lifecycle model, identify configuration, networking, resource, and failure-handling implications, create a feasibility prototype or deployment sketch where practical, and document the approach.
